metadata.label: SPHERE photograph
metadata.coverage: 60 deconvolved VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL frames, camera 1, over 11 nights in 2 apparitions from 2018-04-24 to 2019-08-06, cast onto the ADAM reconstruction the survey released with its rotation record. The camera’s pointing and orientation are computed from that record, JPL Horizons geometry and each frame’s header; the exposure epoch is the midpoint of each frame’s stated exposure, the disc centre is fitted to the limb of the lens mesh, and the sky threshold is one stated fraction of the frame’s peak. With these cameras the mesh reproduces Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.14. Grayscale retains photographed illumination and matched relative frame brightness, each apparition placed through the surface it shares with another, not measured albedo. The grid marks unphotographed, grazing or rejected surface.

transfer.interpretation: Trial acceptance bounds, not estimates of source accuracy. A footprint is the pixel's range times its angular size, so a contributor lies within two of those of the closest source-mesh point, and that point must be visible from the stated camera in the full mesh.

celestial.sunSource: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and Vernazza et al. (2021) Table A.1 observed pole; arbitrary display phase, not an absolute rotational ephemeris

controls.label: Shape
controls.notes: VLT/SPHERE shape model Neutral gray (#808080 sRGB) is a shared display convention, not measured surface color or albedo.

controls.label: SPHERE photograph
controls.notes: 60 deconvolved VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL frames, 11 nights from 2018-04-24 to 2019-08-06, cast onto the ADAM reconstruction from the same survey. The survey’s rotation record describes that frame, so the photograph rides it rather than the model the Shape view uses. Pointing and orientation are computed from that record, JPL Horizons geometry and each frame’s header, at the midpoint of its exposure; the disc centre is fitted to the limb of the mesh. With these cameras the mesh reproduces Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.14. Grayscale is photographed illumination and matched relative frame brightness, each apparition placed through the surface it shares with another. The deconvolution carries no radiometric calibration, so this is not measured albedo or colour. The grid marks surface that was unphotographed, too grazing, or rejected.

controls.label: Thermal inertia

legend.title: Thermal inertia
legend.meta: J m⁻² K⁻¹ s⁻½ · ALMA 1.3 mm, 2019

controls.notes: How slowly the top centimetres of the surface heat and cool, fitted to ALMA thermal images taken over two-thirds of one rotation on 2019 June 19 (Cambioni et al. 2022). One colour per 5-degree cell at about 30 km resolution; the typical uncertainty is about 130. The authors flag 60 to 120 degrees west in their frame as possibly affected by model artifacts. Placed on the ADAM mesh through the published spin states. The grid marks cells the authors did not map.

controls.label: Dielectric constant
controls.notes: How strongly the near-surface material responds to an electric field, fitted to the same ALMA thermal images (Cambioni et al. 2022); higher values suggest more metal in the regolith. One colour per 5-degree cell at about 30 km resolution; the typical uncertainty is about 2. The authors flag 60 to 120 degrees west in their frame as possibly affected by model artifacts. Placed on the ADAM mesh through the published spin states. The grid marks cells the authors did not map.
